picks.style: roman epic invocation, lyre and low drone, resonant male recitation, stately, processional
picks.why: The most famous opening in Latin literature, complete from first line to the founding of Carthage.

picks.style: ancient mediterranean art song, kithara and soft flute, hushed tenor, gentle, questing
picks.why: The doves guiding Aeneas to the golden bough — pure image, a prayer, and a journey in one passage.

picks.style: latin funeral lament, muted horn and low strings, grieving baritone, slow, keening
picks.why: Evander over the body of Pallas: the strongest self-contained lament in the poem.

picks.style: roman comic drinking song, double pipes, hand drum, two rowdy male voices, brisk, tipsy
picks.why: Two rival slaves sharing one cup and one girl — 'I am you, you are I' is the line the play is remembered for.

picks.style: tavern patter song, plucked lyre and wooden clappers, wry male voice, quick, sly
picks.why: Nuts, beans, figs, olives and a Samian jug: concrete, funny, and a whole philosophy of means in eight lines.

picks.style: georgian parlour lament, harpsichord and viol, clear soprano, slow, bitter
picks.why: Flavia after the smallpox — 'Beauty is fled, and dress is now no more' — her best-known and most unsparing passage.

picks.style: baroque love complaint, continuo and solo violin, expressive soprano, rubato, intimate
picks.why: A complete love complaint built on rising verbs: 'I sigh, I faint, I tremble at your touch.'

picks.style: witty georgian ballad, spinet and light strings, arch mezzo voice, trotting, comic
picks.why: Trochaic ballad stanzas prescribing a lover as medicine for the spleen — already half a song.

picks.style: georgian nocturne elegy, chamber strings and low flute, plaintive tenor, slow, hushed
picks.why: 'Tis night, dead night' — a whole nocturne of stilled forest, glow-worm and sleeping village, in clean quatrains.

picks.style: graveyard ballad, solo guitar and cello, low male voice, mournful, unhurried
picks.why: Ends on the epitaph itself: 'He lov'd, believ'd, and was undone.'

picks.style: pastoral ode with refrain, flute and harpsichord, light tenor, lilting, rueful
picks.why: The bee ranging flower to flower, with a genuine four-line refrain to sing back.

picks.style: grand baroque hymn, chapel organ and trumpet, full choir, broad, exalted
picks.why: 'Author of Being, Source of Light' — a hymn opening that names the god by every name and still holds together.

picks.style: solemn passion hymn, sparse organ and low strings, dark male choir, slow, grave
picks.why: 'Behold the Saviour of Mankind' — Wesley's best-known hymn, with the temple veil tearing at its centre.

picks.style: psalm paraphrase, gallery choir with viols, warm mixed voices, moderate, consoling
picks.why: Psalm 116 in ballad metre: death encompassing round, then release — a complete arc.

picks.style: seventeenth century english protest ballad, fiddle and bodhran, rough unison male chorus, driving, defiant
picks.why: The Diggers' Song itself — built on a shouted refrain, made to be sung by a crowd.

picks.style: levelling folk hymn, hurdy-gurdy and hand drum, mixed rustic voices, steady, rising
picks.why: 'Brave Community When Vallies lye levell with Mountains' — the vision song of the English radicals.

picks.style: contemplative art song, solo piano and cello, restrained baritone, slow, meditative
picks.why: Only candidate; a chain of epigraphs on freedom and fate that reads as a coherent lyric.

picks.style: greek oracular chant, lyre and aulos, single male voice, sparse, incantatory
picks.why: Only candidate; an oracle dividing wedlock from war between the gods — short but whole.
